name: EHR-ReasonCon
alternateName: EHR-ReasonCon: Reasoning-Intensive Consistency Verification Between Clinical Notes and Structured Tables in Electronic Health Records
description: EHR-ReasonCon is a reasoning-intensive benchmark for verifying consistency between unstructured clinical notes and structured tables in Electronic Health Records. Built on MIMIC-III with expert-guided annotation, it contains 8,042 anchor entities from 105 clinical notes (38 discharge summaries, 33 physician notes, 34 nursing notes), each labeled CONSISTENT or INCONSISTENT against the patient's structured records, together with the per-admission tables (14 MIMIC-III tables) needed to reproduce every judgment. Each note belongs to a distinct hospital admission of a distinct patient. The data is distributed exclusively through PhysioNet under the PhysioNet Credentialed Health Data Use Agreement; it is not mirrored in this repository.
conditionsOfAccess: Restricted (credentialed) access via PhysioNet: credentialed PhysioNet account, CITI 'Data or Specimens Only Research' training, and the signed Data Use Agreement for this project. The underlying MIMIC-III v1.4 tables used by the accompanying code are a separate credentialed PhysioNet dataset (https://physionet.org/content/mimiciii/1.4/).
citeAs: @misc{kwon2026ehrreasoncon_physionet, title={EHR-ReasonCon: Reasoning-Intensive Consistency Verification Between Clinical Notes and Structured Tables in Electronic Health Records (version 1.0.0)}, author={Kwon, Yeonsu and Kim, Jiho and Choi, Junseong and Rabaey, Paloma and Kim, Minseo and Im, Sujeong and Yang, Jeewon and Lee, Jun-Min and Lee, Sangji and Kim, Jiwon and Yoon, Hangyul and Kwon, Hyunwook and Choi, Edward}, year={2026}, publisher={PhysioNet}, doi={10.13026/7m91-3010}, url={https://physionet.org/content/ehr-reasoncon/1.0.0/}}  Paper: Kwon et al. (2026). Towards Error-Free EHRs: Reasoning-Intensive Consistency Verification Between Clinical Notes and Structured Tables in Electronic Health Records. arXiv:2605.26463.

distribution.name: patient-procedure_icd

recordSet.name: notes
recordSet.description: The 105 clinical notes (83 test / 22 valid): one row per note.

field.name: notes/ROW_ID
field.description: NOTEEVENTS row id; the key of the note's annotation JSON

field.name: notes/HADM_ID
field.description: Hospital admission id (float as stored; patient_data folders use the integer form)

field.name: notes/CATEGORY
field.description: Note type: Discharge summary, Physician, or Nursing

field.name: notes/TEXT
field.description: Note body, restricted to the current hospitalization; annotation 'position' indexes TEXT.split('\n')

field.name: notes/ADMITTIME
field.description: Admission timestamp from ADMISSIONS (resolves relative time expressions)

field.name: annotations/note_type
field.description: discharge | physician | nursing

field.name: annotations/split
field.description: test | valid

field.name: annotations/hadm_id
field.description: Admission id of the note

field.name: annotations/row_id
field.description: ROW_ID of the note (joins notes/ROW_ID)

field.name: annotations/entity_index
field.description: Position of the entity within the note's annotation list

field.name: annotations/entity
field.description: Anchor entity text as written in the note

field.name: annotations/data
field.description: JSON list of {table: {column: value}} mapping the note-side value(s) onto table columns

field.name: annotations/label
field.description: consistent | inconsistent

field.name: annotations/entity_type
field.description: 1 = numerical value, 2 = existence-verifiable event, 3 = string / categorical value

field.name: annotations/position
field.description: 0-based line index of the entity in the note body

field.name: annotations/table
field.description: Primary evidence table (e.g. chartevents)

field.name: annotations/evidence_row_ids
field.description: ROW_IDs of the supporting rows in that table

field.name: annotations/consistency_check_path
field.description: Coded trace of the tool-exploration path the annotator followed

field.name: annotations/inconsistent_columns
field.description: For inconsistent entities, the column(s) where the discrepancy occurs

field.name: annotations/almost_consistent
field.description: Yes/No: values differ only negligibly

field.name: annotations/commonsense_medical_none
field.description: c = commonsense reasoning, m = medical knowledge, n = neither

field.name: annotations/medical_knowledge_source
field.description: URL of the clinical reference consulted, when applicable

field.name: annotations/check_db
field.description: Database or guideline consultation was required to reach the label

field.name: annotations/abnormal_case
field.description: Marks an atypical or edge case flagged during annotation
